title: Bias Beyond Demographics: Probing Decision Boundaries in Black-Box LVLMs via Counterfactual VQA

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) on counterfactual VQA image pairs that differ only in a single demographic attribute (e.g., gender, age, race/ethnicity, body characteristics, occupation), measuring pairwise prediction consistency and symmetric refusal rates.

Evaluating LVLM predictions on counterfactual VQA image pairs that alter a single cultural attribute (e.g., historical contexts, daily practices, cultural traditions), measuring pairwise consistency and refusal symmetry.

Probing LVLM decision boundaries using counterfactual image pairs that vary only in environmental settings (e.g., natural, built, or ambient environments), assessing reasoning stability and refusal symmetry.
Evaluating LVLM responses on counterfactual VQA pairs differing in individual or collective social behaviors (e.g., smoking, greeting styles, eye contact) to measure decision consistency.
Generating counterfactual image pairs with isolated changes in aesthetic visual cues (e.g., personal appearance, object design, physical properties) to test model invariance and fairness.
